claims: More than half of Brazilians are overweight and have an associated comorbidity.
Around 20% of Brazilians are already in the obesity range.
Three weight-loss medications are approved in Brazil: liraglutide (Saxenda), semaglutide (Wegovy and Ozempic), and tirzepatide (Mounjaro).
When taking weight-loss medication, individuals feel less hungry and become full more quickly.
Medication alone is not enough to treat obesity.
Assessment of which medication is most appropriate for an individual must be individualized and performed by a physician.
Weight-loss medications are sold only with a prescription.
Improper use of weight-loss medications without medical guidance can cause adverse effects.
People who seek treatment on their own may experience unpleasant side effects, drug interactions, excessive loss of muscle mass, hair loss, brittle nails, malnutrition, and pancreatic toxicity.
Weight-loss medications can help people who need them, but the goal is not to help individuals lose a few pounds for aesthetic reasons; the goal is to restore health and quality of life.
